record.paper_title: Current Unsolved Problems in Planetary Nebulae Research
record.original_question: If the concentric arcs and rings seen around some planetary nebulae and proto-planetary nebulae are signatures of episodic outflows, what physical process sets the recurrence timescale of those episodes, and what causes successive outflows or lobes to change direction between primary and secondary bipolar axes?

evidence.quote: If the 2D concentric rings are the result of episodic outflows, what determines the period of the episodes?
The presence of secondary bipolar lobes along directions different from the primary lobes suggests that episodic outflows could also change directions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Around certain planetary nebulae and proto-planetary nebulae one observes systems of concentric arcs and quasi-circular rings, as well as bipolar lobes that sometimes appear along two distinct symmetry axes (a "primary" and a "secondary" bipolar axis). Assuming that these concentric arcs/rings are imprints of repeated, quasi-periodic mass-loss episodes from the central evolved star (asymptotic giant branch or post-AGB phase), address the following:

(a) Identify the physical mechanism that sets the recurrence timescale between successive mass-loss episodes responsible for the concentric arcs and rings. In particular, determine which stellar process — e.g. thermal pulses of the helium-burning shell, large-amplitude radial pulsations, magnetic activity cycles, hydrodynamical wind instabilities, or binary-companion interactions — produces inter-ring spacings consistent with the observed range of a few hundred to ~2000 years, and derive (or otherwise characterize) the predicted period as a function of stellar parameters.

(b) Identify the physical mechanism that causes successive episodic outflows (jets or bipolar lobes) to change orientation between a primary bipolar axis and a secondary bipolar axis. In particular, determine whether such reorientation is driven by precession of an accretion disk in a binary or triple system, by misalignment between stellar rotation and magnetic axes, by tidal/orbital evolution of a companion, or by another mechanism, and predict the angular relation and timescale between successive lobe directions.

A complete solution should give a self-consistent physical model linking the recurrence period of the rings/arcs to the reorientation of bipolar lobes, with quantitative predictions that can be compared to observed nebular morphologies.
artifact.category_tag: Planetary nebulae and episodic stellar outflows
artifact.status_search_result: Multiple recent observational studies (e.g. Ramos-Larios et al. 2016, 2020; the 2025 MUSE study of IC 418) confirm the existence of concentric rings/arcs with inter-ring spacings of roughly 500–1900 yr and attribute them to quasi-periodic modulations of the AGB wind, but no consensus exists on the underlying driver (thermal pulses, pulsations, magnetic cycles, or binary interactions). The reorientation between primary and secondary bipolar axes is also actively discussed in terms of binary-induced disk precession, but remains unresolved. The problem is therefore considered open.

status_evidence.title: Rings and arcs around evolved stars – I.
status_evidence.snippet: The averaged time lapse between consecutive rings and arcs is estimated to be in the range 500–1200 yr; the AGB wind has quasi-periodic oscillations whose origin remains uncertain.
status_evidence.claim: Recurrence timescale is observationally constrained but its driving mechanism is not settled.

status_evidence.title: Rings and arcs around evolved stars - IV. IC 418 (A&A 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent MUSE observations characterize ring properties and revisit possible formation mechanisms without uniquely identifying the driver.
status_evidence.claim: Active research as of 2025 indicates the mechanism is still under investigation.

status_evidence.title: Planetary Nebulae review (arXiv 2501.07869)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses unsolved problems including the origin of episodic outflows and changes of symmetry axes in PNe.
status_evidence.claim: Reorientation between primary/secondary bipolar lobes remains an open question.
